reopens.head: ac53661c45fa7b44ec9a3100eb21da29d1de4883
reopens.reason: A ~90-file architectural implementation across bundle source, both platforms' live installs, tests, docs, and a version cut -- not a scoped builder round.

correctness.evidence: Ruff check: All checks passed. Mypy check: Success (no issues in 50 source files). Unit tests: Passed. Release verification: 0.7.0 consistent across pyproject.toml, __init__.py, BUILD.bazel. No live references to removed lead/outer-loop-runner roles (7 grep hits all historical/intentional). lead.md and outer-loop-runner.md deleted from both .claude/agents/ and .opencode/agents/. outer-loop-review skill created (222 lines). AI guidelines properly integrated lead framing. Adapter verify claude and opencode both passed. Implementation plan Accepted 2026-09-03. ADR-0044 exists and Accepted. Diff plausibly implements plan: ~90 files, removes agents, creates skill, updates cross-references.

architecture_scope.evidence: architecture-maintainability-specialist confirmed no rejected alternative was reintroduced (no Agent(...) grant, pr-review untouched as a dependency not an absorber, no surviving mode: primary coordination agent) and code-audit's mode: primary genuinely untouched as the plan required. Two non-blocking findings recorded: the retired agents' broader permission bounds (edit: deny, bash allowlist, maxTurns) were never discussed in the ADR beyond the one ADR-0021 gate; and ADAPTER_ROLE_PATHS no longer scans skills, so the --body guard class has no mechanical backstop (verified the live risk is zero: codev slice publish has no --body parameter at all).

correctness.evidence: correctness-tests-specialist found PR41-DEFAULT-AGENT-VALUE-NOT-PROVENANCE: default_agent deletion keys off the string value alone ("lead"/"orchestrator") with no check of the opencode_default_agent_managed provenance flag, deleting a developer's own default_agent named 'lead' -- confirmed against main's prior preserving behavior by reading both versions directly.

error_handling.evidence: correctness-tests-specialist found one non-blocking finding (stale opencode_default_agent_managed lock flag can wedge codev remove with a CoDevError later) but no unhandled-exception or malformed-input gap; existing CoDevError paths for locally-edited managed agents remain intact and are still converted to conflicts by both callers.

maintainability.evidence: architecture-maintainability-specialist: the change deletes a duplicated ~80-line outer-loop protocol copy from ai-agent-guidelines.md and replaces it with a pointer, a net health improvement. Several non-blocking findings recorded (dead default_managed boolean, one genuinely redundant role-list pair vs. three that check different properties, a plan-doc self-contradiction, one pre-existing stale doc now the sole live holdout, a test that lost its original subject, a permission-marker regression test with no live subject, a stale skill-card version string) -- none blocking, all named for follow-up.

rollout.evidence: rollout-specialist traced the full migration path end to end: role-file removal is safe and generic (conflict-not-deletion for local edits, both platforms), default_agent cleanup confirmed in the diff, outer-loop-review skill present in the bundle, scripts/verify_release.py passes, and the CHANGELOG's Upgrading section is accurate against the actual code. One non-blocking finding: no documented rollback/downgrade path from 0.7.0 to 0.6.0.

test_quality.evidence: correctness-tests-specialist found PR41-DEFAULT-AGENT-UNTESTED: zero tests exercise the new default_agent deletion branch on the update path for a prior CoDev-set value, and none exercises the developer-owned-value boundary the regression violates -- confirmed via grep -rn default_agent tests/test_installer.py, four hits, none reaching the new branch.

findings.summary: default_agent removal keys off the string value alone, not the opencode_default_agent_managed provenance flag, so a developer's own default_agent named 'lead' or 'orchestrator' is now deleted -- a regression from main, which explicitly preserved default_agent == 'lead' as a no-op.

findings.location: tests/test_installer.py (no coverage of the update-path deletion branch)
findings.summary: No test exercises default_agent removal for a prior CoDev-set 'lead'/'orchestrator' value on update, and none exercises the developer-owned-value-must-survive boundary finding 1 violates; deleting the whole new if-block leaves all 815 tests green.

The retired agents' frontmatter carried real execution bounds beyond the ADR-0021 permission.task gate the ADR discusses -- edit: deny, a bash allowlist denying raw git commit/push, external_directory: deny, maxTurns, permissionMode: manual. None of these moved anywhere; a skill inherits the ambient session's full permissions. The ADR reasons about the one gate it names and is silent on the rest.

opencode_default_agent_managed is carried forward as True from a pre-0.7.0 lock and never cleared on update, contradicting the code's own comment that CoDev makes no claim over the key going forward. A developer who sets their own default_agent after updating can hit a CoDevError on codev adapter remove, which blocks all deletions.

The mechanical markers that used to verify lead.md/outer-loop-runner.md named the composite verbs (codev slice publish, --selection, codev git mark-ready, etc.) are gone with the files, and nothing scans the new skill for the same invariant -- a future edit dropping one of those verbs from the skill would pass every check.

The 'never pass --body' guard from outer-loop-runner.md's step 6 was dropped when the step became codev slice publish, which structurally has no --body flag, so the live risk is zero -- but ADAPTER_ROLE_PATHS no longer scans skills at all, so this class of guard has no mechanical backstop for any future skill.

default_managed is permanently False now, but still flows through plan_update's OR-with-old-lock logic and _new_lock, and the OpenCodePreparation field name still implies CoDev manages a key it explicitly does not any more. A producer that can only ever emit False is dead code wearing a name that overclaims.

Of the four places the role set is written down, only Justfile's verify-dist and the installer test assert the identical fact (the same sorted .opencode/agents filename list) -- ADAPTER_ROLE_PATHS and OPENCODE_AGENT_CONFIGS hold genuinely different data. The PR description's 'a fourth place' framing overstates the redundancy; only one pair is a true duplicate worth collapsing.

The header says Status: Accepted, but the closing section still reads 'this document's Status line is still Draft. It becomes buildable once that line reads Accepted' -- commit dc5b1ce fixed the header and missed the trailer, leaving the authority document asserting two contradictory things about its own status.

findings.location: docs/for-ai/ai-agent-guidelines.md (pre-existing, orphaned by an earlier docs relocation)
findings.summary: This file still describes lead dispatching builder/code-audit-gate and handing to outer-loop-runner. Pre-existing debt, out of ADR-0044's literal scope, but after this PR it is the only live document in the repository still asserting the removed model -- in tension with this PR's own commit message claiming every cross-reference was fixed.

Unchanged by this diff, but its meaning changed underneath it: it used to pin the managed-name-collision path for lead specifically; with lead no longer managed, it now only proves an unrelated key survives a merge that never inspects it.

The scanner's own comment now says nothing currently in scope should match it; the regression test had to relocate onto builder, a role that would never carry this permission block, so the test proves the scanner works rather than that a real invariant holds. Worth one CHANGELOG sentence so a future reader does not 'restore' it by re-adding a permission block somewhere.
Says 'currently 0.6.0' in the PR that cuts 0.7.0. Pre-existing pattern (all 15 other skill cards say 0.3.0), but the new card joined it already wrong.

summary: Plan: lead becomes a skill, not an agent, on every platform
